samples.summary: Revocation reconcile can never purge an archive: it enumerates candidates from HEADERS, and archiving deletes the header
samples.evidence:
`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` builds its candidate set from `store.storedDocumentIds()` (offline-erase.ts:351). `storedDocumentIds()` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:930-942) reads only the HEADERS object store via `headerKeysWhere(BY_USER, ...)`. But `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` — the only thing that writes an archive — deletes the header in the same transaction (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:810). So a document that has been archived has no header, is never listed by `storedDocumentIds()`, is never passed to `purgeDocument(id, {archives: 'drop'})`, and its archive is therefore unreachable by this reconcile.

This is the only cleanup path that runs on the *removed member's own* device — `deleteWorkspace`/`removeMember` in api/workspaces.ts purge on the requester's device, and the design says so explicitly: "The removed member's own device is reached by nothing that happens here, so it reconciles on its own ... `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`". The design also states the rule this breaks: "a membership revoked while an archive survives would hand the user a permanent copy of content they may no longer read."

Vector: a workspace document acquires an archive (any `LocalChangesDropped` — server-side compaction/epoch-reanchor is the common one), then the user is removed from that workspace. The archive holds the full gzip'd document snapshot, including content authored by others. On the next session `OfflineRuntime` skips it in the reconcile and then *offers* it via `offerRecoverableWork`; accepting calls `recoverOfflineCopy`, which creates a brand-new document owned by the now-removed user containing that workspace's content. Only the 30-day `collectStale` sweep ever removes it.

samples.summary: Revocation reconcile bails out on an empty accessible list — exactly the shape a fully-revoked user produces
samples.evidence:
`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` returns 0 when `accessible.length === 0` (offline-erase.ts:339-344). The stated justification is "A user who genuinely has no documents has nothing stored either" — that reasoning is inverted for the one case this function exists to handle.

`GET /documents` (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180-195) returns documents across the caller's workspace memberships. A user whose stored offline copies all came from workspace W, and who is then removed from W, gets `[]` back on the next session if they hold no other documents. The guard then refuses to purge anything, so every local copy of W's documents — full document content they may no longer read — stays on the disk until the 30-day `collectStale` sweep. The same empty answer is also what a legitimately-revoked-from-everything user produces, so the guard cannot distinguish the safe case from the exact unsafe one.

The caller (`OfflineRuntime`, components/offline-runtime.tsx) already separates a *failed* listing (which throws before reaching here) from a successful empty one, so the successful-empty case could be honoured safely.

samples.summary: `isOpenInAnyTab` matches a lock held by any account, so another user's open tab defers this user's revocation purge
samples.evidence:
`isOpenInAnyTab` matches `lock.name.startsWith("wb-durable:") && lock.name.endsWith(`:${documentKeyOf(key)}`)` — the `{userId}` segment of `wb-durable:{userId}:{docKey}` is deliberately not matched (durable-session.test.ts asserts "reports a document held by any tab as open ... the user segment is not matched").

`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` passes `isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab` and `skipOpen: true` into `purgeDocument` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:886). So on a shared device where account B has `sheet-7` open in another tab, account A's revoked local copy of `sheet-7` is skipped and survives that session. Sparing is the safe direction for eviction, but here it is gating a security cleanup: content whose read authority has been revoked is retained because a *different* account has the document open. It retries next session, so the window is bounded rather than permanent.

samples.summary: Recovery is offered even when the revocation reconcile failed, so un-purged archives are handed back in that session
samples.evidence: In `OfflineRuntime`'s effect the reconcile is wrapped in `try { ... } catch (err) { console.warn(...) }` and execution falls straight through to `offerRecoverableWork(...)`. A failed `fetchDocuments()` (offline, 5xx, rate limit) therefore skips the only purge that removes archives for revoked documents, and the very next statement offers every archive back as a document the user can materialize. The suite even pins this ordering as intended ("keeps sweeping when the reconcile fails" asserts `toastWarning` fires after `fetchDocuments.mockRejectedValue`). Compounding finding 1: on the removed member's device the reconcile is the only authority check in the loop, and the recovery offer does not require it to have succeeded.

samples.summary: Path-traversal regression assertion weakened from every request to some request, and this diff added the companion request that satisfies it
samples.evidence:
The per-call assertion changed from `for (const raw of urls) { expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL)) }` to `expect(paths.some(p => p.includes(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL)))).toBe(true)`. The negative traversal check is still applied to every path, so the core property holds — but the positive "this route encoded the id into its own path segment" check is now satisfiable by any one request in the batch.

That matters because this same diff is what introduced the companion request: `deleteWorkspace` and `removeMember` now call `documentIdsIn(ref)` → `fetchWorkspace(ref)` (api/workspaces.ts), which puts the encoded id in a path all on its own. So for the `workspaces: delete` and `workspaces: remove member` cases, the assertion is now satisfied by `fetchWorkspace` regardless of how the DELETE itself builds its URL — e.g. a regression that moved the id into a query string, or dropped it, would no longer be caught by this check. Scoping the `some` to the mutating request, or asserting a minimum count, would restore the coverage without failing on the id-less `fetchDocuments` call.

samples.summary: `isDocument` suffix match is over-broad, so a purge for one document id can delete another document's entries and archives
samples.evidence:
`isDocument(key, documentId)` returns true when `documentKeyOf(key) === documentId || docKey.endsWith(`-${documentId}`)`. The suffix arm is unanchored at the prefix: any stored key whose document key happens to end in `-<documentId>` matches. It drives `purgeDocument` (live entries) and `dropArchivesForDocument` (archives, which are the only copy of unreconciled work), both reached from `purgeOfflineDocuments` on a server-accepted delete and from the revocation reconcile.

With opaque UUID document ids a collision is unlikely, but nothing constrains the id shape at this boundary — `deleteDocuments` passes straight through whatever the server echoed in `result.deleted`, and `storedDocumentIds()` derives ids by slicing at the *first* dash, so a key without the expected `type-id` shape yields an id that can then suffix-match other keys. Anchoring on the known type prefixes (the same table `describeArchivedDocument` already keeps) would make the match exact.

samples.summary: `collectStale` destroys other accounts' archives from whichever account happens to be signed in
samples.evidence: `collectStale` sweeps live entries across every account (`headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` with no user filter, line 1115) and then calls `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` with `onlyUser` left undefined (line 1129), so it deletes every account's archives past the cutoff. The comments argue this deliberately, and the same 30-day policy is applied uniformly — but the effect is that a session authenticated as user A performs an irreversible destructive action on user B's only copy of work the server never took, and `listArchives`/`loadArchive`/`evictOldest` are all careful to refuse exactly that data to A. `dropArchivesWhere` already accepts an `onlyUser` parameter that is never passed by any caller, so the scoped alternative exists and is unused. Worth an explicit decision record rather than leaving the asymmetry implicit.

samples.summary: Logout now awaits an IndexedDB erase before redirecting, so a stalled open leaves the UI signed in after the server session is gone
samples.evidence: `logout()` awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout(...)` before the `redirectTo("/login")` that follows, and `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm awaits the same thing before its redirect. `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` catches rejections, but it cannot bound a *hang*: `WafflebaseDocStore.open()` only settles on `onsuccess`/`onerror`/`onblocked`, and a connection that never fires any of those (storage pressure, a wedged profile, an extension-blocked database) leaves the promise pending forever. The POST to `/auth/logout` has already cleared the server session at that point, so the tab stays on an authenticated-looking page indefinitely with no session behind it, and no pending-erase marker is recorded (that only happens in the `catch`). A timeout race around the erase would keep the redirect unconditional.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments derives its candidate set solely from store.storedDocumentIds() (offline-erase.ts:351), which reads only the HEADERS store via headerKeysWhere (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:930-942, :1221-1231). WafflebaseDocStore.remove() — the only writer of archives (:802) — deletes the header in the same transaction (:810), so an archived document has an ARCHIVES row and no HEADERS row and is therefore never passed to purgeDocument(id, {archives:"drop"}) (:356). No other revocation-time archive cleanup exists: dropArchivesForDocument (:945) is only reachable through purgeDocument, dropAllForUser is logout/toggle-off, and collectStale drops archives only by age (:1129). The existing "archives included" test passes only because it re-seeds the header after remove() (offline-erase.test.ts:389), so the archive-only shape is uncovered. Downstream there is no access re-check: listRecoverableWork (offline-copy.ts:58-68) maps every archive, offline-runtime.tsx:144/204-209 offers it (a failed fetchDocument only changes the title), and recoverOfflineCopy (offline-copy-recovery.ts:175-213) creates a new document from the archive without any authorization check. Content survives revocation on the removed member's own device and can be re-materialized as a document they own — in-lane access-control/data-exposure defect, real and unguarded.

finding.summary: Revocation reconcile cannot see archive-only documents, so content from a workspace the user was removed from is never erased
finding.evidence:
`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` builds its candidate list with `store.storedDocumentIds()` (offline-erase.ts:351), and that method enumerates only the `headers` object store (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:930-942, `headerKeysWhere(BY_USER, ...)`). But `remove()` deletes the header and writes the content into the separate `archives` store — so a document that hit `LocalChangesDropped` has an archive and NO header. It is therefore absent from `storedDocumentIds()`, `purgeDocument(id, {archives:'drop'})` is never called for it, and the archive survives the reconcile.

This is the exact case the design says the reconcile exists for. `workspaces.ts` removeMember documents that the removed member's own device "is reached by nothing that happens here, so it reconciles on its own: OfflineRuntime asks the server what it may still read on every session and drops what is no longer listed (purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments)". For an archived document that promise is not kept.

Chain: user A opens sheet-X in workspace W; the SDK hits one of the three LocalChangesDropped paths, so the full compressed document moves to `archives`. An owner removes A from W. On A's next session purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments sees no header for sheet-X and drops nothing. OfflineRuntime's recovery toast then offers the archive back and recoverOfflineCopy creates `sheet-X (offline copy)` — a permanent, server-side document A owns, containing content from a workspace A was removed from.

The existing test misses it because it re-seeds the live entry after archiving: offline-erase.test.ts "drops what the server no longer lists, archives included" calls store.remove(...) and then `await seed(store, "pk/wb:1:sheet-gone/sheet-gone")` again, restoring the header the real scenario would not have. The archive-only shape is untested.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:351) derives its candidate set solely from `store.storedDocumentIds()`, and that method (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:930-942) enumerates only the HEADERS store via `headerKeysWhere(BY_USER, ...)`. `remove()` on a loss path (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:791-811) writes an ArchiveRecord into ARCHIVES and deletes the header in the same transaction, so a LocalChangesDropped document has an archive and no header. Such a document is therefore never passed to `purgeDocument(id, {archives:"drop"})` (offline-erase.ts:356) and `dropArchivesForDocument` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:945-961) — the only archive deleter on this path, called only from purgeDocument:902-904 — never runs for it. No downstream guard exists: `listRecoverableWork` (offline-copy.ts:58-68) maps `listArchives()` with no comparison against the `accessible` list fetched at offline-runtime.tsx:128, and offline-runtime.tsx:211-256 then offers `recoverOfflineCopy`, materializing a new server-side document from content in a workspace the user was removed from. The existing test does re-seed the header after archiving (offline-erase.test.ts:388-389), so the archive-only shape is genuinely untested. This is an access-control gap in the Security lane: a revocation gate that reads as covering archives but is bypassed for a reachable record shape.

finding.summary: isOpenInAnyTab fails open as "open" for the erasure callers, silently disabling both the revocation purge and the 30-day sweep on browsers with LockManager.request but no query
finding.evidence:
isOpenInAnyTab returns `true` — meaning "assume open, do not delete" — both when supportsDurableSession() is false (durable-session.ts:211-213) and when navigator.locks.query() throws (durable-session.ts:228-230). That default is correct for its original caller, eviction, where refusing to delete costs a failed write. It is inverted for the two erasure callers, where refusing to delete costs retained content the user is no longer entitled to.

Reachability is not hypothetical, because the capability probe and the call disagree about which API they need. supportsDurableSession() checks only `typeof navigator.locks.request === "function"` (durable-session.ts:57-65); it never probes `query`. On a runtime shipping LockManager.request but not LockManager.query, durability is ENABLED — entries and archives get written — while line 215 throws TypeError on every call and the catch answers `true` forever.

Consequences, both permanent on such a runtime:
- purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments passes `skipOpen: true` and `isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab` (offline-erase.ts:356, offline-runtime.tsx), so purgeDocument's `if (options.skipOpen && (await this.isLive(key))) continue;` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:886) skips EVERY entry. Access revoked by someone else is never cleaned up.
- collectStale's isLive check skips every live entry for the same reason, so the 30-day backstop the design's cleanup table names as the catch-all for every other row never collects anything.

A transient query() rejection costs one sweep; the missing-query case costs all of them. Fix is to fail in the safe direction per caller — erasure should treat "cannot tell" as "not open" — or require `query` in supportsDurableSession() so durability is refused where the guard cannot work.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. isOpenInAnyTab fails open to `true` both when supportsDurableSession() is false (durable-session.ts:211-213) and when navigator.locks.query() rejects/throws (durable-session.ts:214-230). supportsDurableSession() probes only `navigator.locks.request` (durable-session.ts:61-65) and never `query`, so a runtime with request-but-no-query enables durability (entries/archives are written) while every isOpenInAnyTab call throws TypeError at line 215 and the catch answers `true` forever. Both erasure callers consume that answer: offline-runtime.tsx:132 -> offline-erase.ts:356-359 (`skipOpen: true`) -> wafflebase-doc-store.ts:886 skips every matching entry, and offline-runtime.tsx:70/101 -> collectStale's isLive guard at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1118 skips every entry. Net effect: the revocation purge deletes no live entries and the 30-day backstop collects nothing. This is in the security lane as sensitive-data retention past revocation — the repo's own design states content "must not outlive the authority to read it" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:839-840, docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:260-271) and names the sweep as the catch-all backstop (design 255, 273-280). Minor overstatement in the finding (archives ARE dropped unconditionally at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:902-904; only live entries are retained) does not refute it. No guard elsewhere normalizes "cannot tell" to "not open" for the erasure callers, so I have no named refutation ground.
